Decide the type size and the page orientation for one table

Source: R/quarto-table.R
apa_layout_decide.Rd

The ladder of D7/D7b, run on an exact width rather than a search: 10 pt upright; if that does not fit, ROTATE and stay at 10 pt; if it still does not fit, shrink by closed-form calculation. If that goes below 6 pt, use it anyway so that nothing is ever cut off, and warn.

Usage

apa_layout_decide(
  plan,
  geom = NULL,
  geom_landscape = NULL,
  landscape = NA,
  can_execute_rotation = TRUE,
  size = NULL,
  col_overhead_in = 0
)

Arguments

plan

a display plan, from `apa_display_plan()`.

geom

optional page geometry, from `apa_page_geometry("portrait")`; read from the document being rendered when not supplied.

geom_landscape

optional rotated-page geometry, from `apa_page_geometry("landscape")`.

landscape

Tri-state. `TRUE` forces a rotated page, `FALSE` forbids one (the table is shrunk to the upright page instead, keeping every column), `NA` (the default) lets measurement decide. Resolved by [apa_landscape_request()] from the chunk option and the builder argument before it reaches here.

can_execute_rotation

`FALSE` when apaquarto cannot carry out a rotation on this render. A DIFFERENT fact from `landscape = FALSE`: one is the user declining a rotated page, the other is the render being unable to produce one, and only the first is anybody's choice.

size

an explicit point size (D26), overriding the whole rotate-then-shrink ladder – because the caller already fixed the size, shrinking is no longer an option, so the ONLY question left is whether the page needs to rotate to hold it. `NULL` (default) runs the ladder exactly as before this parameter existed: this codepath is provably unreached when `size` is `NULL`, so the default case is byte-identical to the pre-D26 behaviour. Fix round 1 (Task 8): before this parameter existed, an explicit `font.size` reached the LaTeX emitter with NO re-check at all – `apa.cor.table(attitude)` at 20 pt measures 10.26 in against a 6.5 in upright page and rendered with no warning and no rotation. `size` closes that gap by deciding rotation from the SIZE ACTUALLY EMITTED rather than the ladder's own 10 pt guess. It keeps exactly the one warning that remains true whatever size was requested: a table whose `\tabcolsep` alone exceeds even the rotated budget cannot be rescued by ANY size, explicit or automatic.

col_overhead_in

fixed per-column overhead in inches that the destination adds to every column whatever the type size, and that the content model therefore cannot see. `0` (the default) for LaTeX, whose own `\tabcolsep` term is already in the model; the Word render passes `APA_WORD_CELL_PADDING_IN` (B6 option 2, Phase 1.12), the bundled styles' fixed `<w:tblCellMar>`. Charged on the WIDTH side – it is part of the space the table really occupies – so every budget in a warning is still the true page width.

Value

a list with `size` (points), `rotate` (logical), `fits` (did the chosen size actually fit its page) and `width` (the predicted width at `size`, in inches, `col_overhead_in` included).

Why the fit is re-checked rather than assumed

`apa_size_for_width()` bottoms out at `APA_LATEX_MIN_EMITTABLE_SIZE` and returns that size even when it does not fit – which it cannot, for a table whose font-independent `\tabcolsep` and per-column rounding alone exceed the page. So the returned size is not evidence of a fit. This function computes the width it actually gets and tests that, which is also what makes the warning able to distinguish "small but complete" from "still too wide, and no size can fix it".

One measurement, not one per candidate

`apa_latex_natural_width()` re-runs flextable's `autofit()` every time it is called (measured: 0.66 s on a 14-column table). The per-column content vector is therefore measured ONCE here, by `apa_latex_content_at_12()`, and every candidate size – including the one `apa_size_for_width()` solves for – is computed from that same vector.
